pundit.name: Eric Wynalda
pundit.take:
Gunner is the only one in this fantasy pool who has any idea what he’s doing, while Rafe's picks are like a blindfolded monkey throwing darts at a map. Let's start with Brazil versus Norway in East Rutherford. Mustard Boy, a.k.a. Zach, really went for a Tier 1 giant in Brazil, hoping their samba style would save his lackluster draft. But when your support teams are Austria and Saudi Arabia, it's clear you drafted like a tourist, not a tactician. Expect Brazil to trample over Devin's Norway, who’s still trying to figure out if they're a contender or just there for the meatballs. Gunner's France and Morocco are putting others to shame with consistent performances and tactical choices — that's a guy who drafted with insight, unlike the rest of these amateurs.

Turning to Mexico against England, let's talk about The Noisemaker. Rafe picked Germany first but backed it up with nothing more than chaos, like Tunisia and Uzbekistan — does he even know where those countries are on a map? Meanwhile, England’s got Gayden, the self-proclaimed Backpass Assassin, whose draft strategy was to pick random teams with cool flags. Watch as Mexico struggles to find the goal against an England side that can't keep a clean sheet against a junior varsity team. It's time for these managers to take notes: Gunner’s roster is all but wearing the crown already, proving that competence beats cluelessness every time.
